request.query: Simultaneous approximation of finitely many positive reals by scaled natural ceilings with arbitrary multiplicative error and strict separation margin.

      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (ξ : ℝ) {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∃ j k, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ ↑n ∧ |↑k * ξ - ↑j| ≤ 1 / (↑n + 1)",

      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} (n : ℕ) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) {ε : ℝ},\n  0 < ε →\n    ∀ {b : R},\n      b ≠ 0 →\n        ∀ (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ n).succ → Fin n → R),\n          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : Fin n), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε",

      "type": "∀ (ξ : ℝ) {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∃ k, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ |↑k * ξ - ↑(round (↑k * ξ))| ≤ 1 / (↑n + 1)",
      "informal_description": "For any real number $\\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exists a natural number $k$ satisfying $1 \\leq k \\leq n$ such that the absolute difference between $k\\xi$ and the nearest integer is at most $\\frac{1}{n + 1}$, i.e., $\\left| k\\xi - \\text{round}(k\\xi) \\right| \\leq \\frac{1}{n + 1}$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.NumberTheory.DiophantineApproximation.Basic"

    {
      "formal_name": "AbsoluteValue.IsAdmissible.exists_approx",
      "informal_name": "Existence of Approximate Solutions under Admissible Absolute Values",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ},\n  0 < ε →\n    ∀ {b : R},\n      b ≠ 0 →\n        ∀ (h : abv.IsAdmissible) (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ Fintype.card ι).succ → ι → R),\n          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : ι), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε",
      "informal_description": "For any finite set $\\iota$, positive real number $\\varepsilon$, non-zero element $b$ in a Euclidean domain $R$ equipped with an admissible absolute value, and a function $A : \\text{Fin}(N) \\to \\iota \\to R$ (where $N = (\\text{card}(\\varepsilon)^{\\#\\iota} + 1)$), there exist distinct indices $i_0$ and $i_1$ such that for all $k$, the absolute value of the difference between the remainders $A(i_1, k) \\bmod b$ and $A(i_0, k) \\bmod b$ is strictly less than $\\varepsilon \\cdot |b|$. This result leverages the pigeonhole principle and properties of admissible absolute values compatible with the Euclidean division algorithm.",

    {

      "informal_name": "Existence of Positive Constants for Liouville Numbers with Exponent p",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {p x : ℝ},\n  LiouvilleWith p x →\n    ∃ C, ∃ (_ : 0 < C), ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ m, x ≠ ↑m / ↑n ∧ |x - ↑m / ↑n| < C / ↑n ^ p",
      "informal_description": "For a real number $x$ that is a Liouville number with exponent $p$, there exists a positive real constant $C$ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $n$, there exists an integer $m$ where $x \\neq \\frac{m}{n}$ and the absolute difference $\\left|x - \\frac{m}{n}\\right|$ is less than $\\frac{C}{n^p}$.",

      "informal_name": "Liouville number with exponent p",

      "informal_description": "A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ where $ x \neq \frac{m}{n} $ and the absolute difference $ |x - \frac{m}{n}| $ is less than $ \frac{C}{n^p} $.",

items.informal_name: Existence of Integer Approximations for Real Numbers with Bounded Denominator
items.informal_description: For any real number $\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exist integers $j$ and $k$ such that $0 < k \leq n$ and $|k\xi - j| \leq \frac{1}{n + 1}$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Approximating Indices for Admissible Absolute Values
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} (n : ℕ) (h : abv.IsAdmissible) {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : R},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ n).succ → Fin n → R),
          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : Fin n), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, admissible absolute value $\abv$, positive real $\varepsilon$, nonzero element $b \in R$, and function $A : \mathrm{Fin}(\abv.\mathrm{card}(\varepsilon)^n + 1) \times \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to R$, there exist distinct indices $i_0, i_1$ such that for all $k$, the absolute value of $A(i_1, k) \bmod b - A(i_0, k) \bmod b$ is less than $\abv(b) \cdot \varepsilon$.

items.informal_name: Existence of a Natural Number with Bounded Diophantine Approximation
items.informal_description: For any real number $\xi$ and positive integer $n$, there exists a natural number $k$ satisfying $1 \leq k \leq n$ such that the absolute difference between $k\xi$ and the nearest integer is at most $\frac{1}{n + 1}$, i.e., $\left| k\xi - \text{round}(k\xi) \right| \leq \frac{1}{n + 1}$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Approximate Solutions under Admissible Absolute Values
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : EuclideanDomain R] {abv : AbsoluteValue R ℤ} {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ∀ {b : R},
      b ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (h : abv.IsAdmissible) (A : Fin (h.card ε ^ Fintype.card ι).succ → ι → R),
          ∃ i₀ i₁, i₀ ≠ i₁ ∧ ∀ (k : ι), ↑(abv (A i₁ k % b - A i₀ k % b)) < abv b • ε
items.informal_description: For any finite set $\iota$, positive real number $\varepsilon$, non-zero element $b$ in a Euclidean domain $R$ equipped with an admissible absolute value, and a function $A : \text{Fin}(N) \to \iota \to R$ (where $N = (\text{card}(\varepsilon)^{\#\iota} + 1)$), there exist distinct indices $i_0$ and $i_1$ such that for all $k$, the absolute value of the difference between the remainders $A(i_1, k) \bmod b$ and $A(i_0, k) \bmod b$ is strictly less than $\varepsilon \cdot |b|$. This result leverages the pigeonhole principle and properties of admissible absolute values compatible with the Euclidean division algorithm.

items.informal_name: Existence of Positive Constants for Liouville Numbers with Exponent p
items.type:
∀ {p x : ℝ},
  LiouvilleWith p x →
    ∃ C, ∃ (_ : 0 < C), ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ m, x ≠ ↑m / ↑n ∧ |x - ↑m / ↑n| < C / ↑n ^ p
items.informal_description: For a real number $x$ that is a Liouville number with exponent $p$, there exists a positive real constant $C$ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $n$, there exists an integer $m$ where $x \neq \frac{m}{n}$ and the absolute difference $\left|x - \frac{m}{n}\right|$ is less than $\frac{C}{n^p}$.

A real number $ x $ is called a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if there exists a positive constant $ C $ such that for infinitely many natural numbers $ n $, there exists an integer $ m $ where $ x 
eq  rac{m}{n} $ and the absolute difference $ |x -  rac{m}{n}| $ is less than $  rac{C}{n^p} $.

items.informal_name: Liouville Numbers with Exponent Greater Than Two Are Contained in a Union of Approximation Sets
items.type:
{x | ∃ p > 2, LiouvilleWith p x} ⊆
  ⋃ m,
    (fun x => x + ↑m) ⁻¹'
      ⋃ n, ⋃ (_ : n > 0), {x | ∃ᶠ (b : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ Finset.Icc 0 ↑b, |x - ↑a / ↑b| < 1 / ↑b ^ (2 + 1 / ↑n)}
items.informal_description: The set of real numbers $ x $ that are Liouville numbers with some exponent $ p > 2 $ is contained in the union over all integers $ m $ and natural numbers $ n > 0 $ of the preimages under translation by $ m $ of the sets where, for infinitely many $ b $, there exists an integer $ a $ between $ 0 $ and $ b $ such that $ |x - \frac{a}{b}| < \frac{1}{b^{2 + 1/n}} $.

items.informal_name: Frequent Rational Approximation of Liouville Numbers
items.type: ∀ {x : ℝ}, Liouville x → ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ᶠ (b : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ a, x ≠ ↑a / ↑b ∧ |x - ↑a / ↑b| < 1 / ↑b ^ n
items.informal_description:
For any Liouville number $x$ and every natural number $n$, there exist infinitely many natural numbers $b$ and integers $a$ such that $x 
eq  rac{a}{b}$ and $\left|x -  rac{a}{b}\right| <  rac{1}{b^n}$.
